citations.quote: The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, fix a positive real action-scale parameter
$\hbar>0$, and let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.

Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, contraction maps
$\Psi_f^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$ and core operators $S_\pm(f)$ on the
finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), with
completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$,
Fock space $F(H)$ and finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]].

Let $n\ge1$ and $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$, with the componentwise integral and quotient conventions of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]. Define
$$\widehat f(\xi)=\mathcal Ff(\xi):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(x)\exp(-2\pi i x\cdot\xi)\,dx,\qquad \xi\in\mathbb R^n.$$
Here $x\cdot\xi=\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\xi_j$, Lebesgue measure is used, and the exponential is [[def-complex-exponential]]. Its unit modulus follows from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The integral is evaluated using any measurable representative. Absolute convergence and representative independence are the obligations discharged by [[lem-l-one-fourier-transform-is-well-defined]]. The output is a function defined at every frequency, not merely an almost-everywhere class. At frequency zero the formula reads $\widehat f(0)=\int f$. No choice selection of representatives for a family of classes is part of this definition.

Assume countable choice and let $n\ge1$. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry $\mathcal F_2:L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.
Assume countable choice. The Fourier transform is a topological automorphism of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, with $\mathcal F^2=R$ and $\mathcal F^{-1}=R\mathcal F$, where $Rf(x)=f(-x)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. If $f : V \to \mathbb C$ belongs to $L^1(\lambda_n)$,
then
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge0$, $\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and use the symplectic
form $\omega((q,p),(q',p'))=q\cdot p'-p\cdot q'$ on $\mathbb R^{2n}$. On
$L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ define

$$\big(S_\lambda(q,p,t)f\big)(x) =e^{i\lambda t+i\lambda p\cdot(x-q/2)}f(x-q).$$
Then $S_\lambda$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of [[def-heisenberg-group-of-a-symplectic-vector-space]], has central character $t\mapsto e^{i\lambda t}$, and its Weyl operators form an irreducible regular Weyl system with phase $e^{-i\lambda\omega/2}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real
symplectic vector space of dimension $2n$, let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be
nonzero, and let $W:V\to U(\mathcal H)$ be a nonzero irreducible regular
Weyl system with

$$W(v)W(w)=e^{-i\lambda\omega(v,w)/2}W(v+w).$$
Then $W$ is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger Weyl system on $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$, so there is exactly one unitary-equivalence class of irreducible regular Weyl systems with the fixed parameter $\lambda$. In a symplectic basis the model is
$$\big(W_\lambda(q,p)f\big)(x)=e^{i\lambda p\cdot(x-q/2)}f(x-q),$$
for $\omega((q,p),(q',p'))=q\cdot p'-p\cdot q'$. The statement assumes finite-dimensional phase space, irreducibility, strong continuity, and a fixed nonzero central parameter. It makes no claim about algebraic modules, nonregular representations, $\lambda=0$, or infinitely many modes.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

derivations.claim:
On $L^2(\mathbb R^r)$, multiplication by real $x_j$ is symmetric. If $g$
lies in its adjoint domain with adjoint value $h$, testing against compactly
supported functions on each box where $x_j$ is bounded gives $h=x_jg$ almost
everywhere there; the boxes exhaust $\mathbb R^r$, so $x_jg\in L^2$ and the
adjoint domain is exactly $D(M_{x_j})$. Thus $M_{x_j}$ is self-adjoint. Let
$Dg(k):=(2\pi)^{-r/2}g(k/(2\pi))$. The L1 Fourier definition in [F2] gives,
for $f\in\mathcal S$, $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ang}}f=D\mathcal F_{2\pi}f$ by
substitution in the defining integrals. For every $g\in L^2$, [F2] and the
change-of-variables formula in [F2] give
$$\|Dg\|_2^2=(2\pi)^{-r}\int|g(k/(2\pi))|^2\,dk=\int|g(\xi)|^2\,d\xi,$$
so $D$ is an isometry; its inverse is $D^{-1}h(\xi)=(2\pi)^{r/2}h(2\pi\xi)$,
so it is unitary. For Schwartz seminorms
$p_{\alpha,\beta}(g)=\sup_k|k^\alpha\partial^\beta g(k)|$,
$$p_{\alpha,\beta}(Dg)=(2\pi)^{|\alpha|-|\beta|-r/2}p_{\alpha,\beta}(g),$$
and the corresponding inverse formula has finite reciprocal factors. Hence
$D$ and $D^{-1}$ are continuous on Schwartz space. Together with [F2] this
proves that $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ang}}$ is unitary on $L^2$ and a topological
automorphism of Schwartz space. Conjugating $M_{k_j}$ by it defines the
self-adjoint operator $-i\partial_{x_j}$; on Schwartz functions the kernel
formula and integration by parts give
$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ang}}(-i\partial_{x_j}f)=k_j\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ang}}f$.
Schwartz functions are a core for multiplication: truncate by smooth compact
cutoffs and then mollify on the resulting bounded support; dominated
convergence controls $f$ and $x_jf$, and boundedness of $x_j$ on that support
controls the mollification error. Fourier invariance of Schwartz space gives
the same core assertion for the derivative. Conjugation by $\mathcal U$
therefore defines the stated self-adjoint quadratures and common core.

On that core, [F1] gives $Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*)$ and
$P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$. The creation and annihilation CCR in
[F1] imply the displayed quadrature commutators by bilinearity; all products are defined on
the finite Hermite span. Direct multiplication of the formula for $W$ gives
the phase $e^{-i\hbar(q\cdot p'-p\cdot q')/2}$, which is
$e^{-i\hbar z^TJz'/2}$ in interleaved notation. Its strong continuity and
irreducibility follow from [F3] after the parameter-preserving change
$(q_0,p_0)=(-\sqrt\hbar p,q/\sqrt\hbar)$ in the root Schrödinger formula.
The real symplectic form is unchanged by that map and the central parameter
is $\hbar\ne0$. Applying [F5] proves the representation-equivalence clause
with precisely its hypotheses.

The positive trace-class spectral expansion in [F6] has weights summing
to one. For any eigenvalue $w>0$, changing the orthonormal basis of its
eigenspace changes the sum of squared norms $\sum\|R_j\psi\|^2$ by a unitary
finite-dimensional change of basis when the eigenspace is finite-dimensional;
positive trace-class compactness makes each nonzero eigenspace finite
dimensional. The same basis invariance holds for the sesquilinear cross sum
by polarization, and the zero eigenspace contributes nothing. Cauchy–Schwarz
then gives absolute convergence of each first-moment series and of each
cross-moment series under the stated second-moment bound. Thus the definitions
of $d,V$ are finite and basis independent; taking the real part makes
$V_{jk}=V_{kj}\in\mathbb R$. Finally, every finite-dimensional cutoff of
Fock space has finite matrix dimension, and for square matrices $A,B$,
$\operatorname{tr}(AB-BA)=0$ by expanding the diagonal entries, whereas the
identity has positive trace. Hence a finite cutoff cannot satisfy the exact
CCR $[Q_j,P_j]=i\hbar I$.

$$q_{A,V}[u]=\frac1{2m}\sum_{j=1}^d\|(-i\hbar\partial_j-qA_j)u\|_2^2+\int_{\mathbb R^d}V|u|^2,\qquad u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C).$$

$$B_\perp(x,y)=\partial_xA_y(x,y)-\partial_yA_x(x,y),$$
in teslas. Thus $A=(0,Bx)$ gives $B_\perp=B$ for a constant signed scalar
$B$. In $d=3$, for coordinates $(x,y,z)$ and $A=(A_x,A_y,A_z)$, define the
field vector $\mathbf B:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ in teslas by
$$\mathbf B=(\partial_yA_z-\partial_zA_y,\ \partial_zA_x-\partial_xA_z,\ \partial_xA_y-\partial_yA_x)=\nabla\times A.$$

For a core spinor $u=(u_1,u_2)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2)$,
define the spin-independent form
$$q^{(2)}_{A,V}[u]=q_{A,V}[u_1]+q_{A,V}[u_2].$$

form
$$q^{\mathrm P}_{A,V,g}[u]=q^{(2)}_{A,V}[u]-\frac{gq}{2m}\int_{\mathbb R^3}u(x)^*(S\cdot\mathbf B(x))u(x)\,dx,$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ (A function is a relation $f$ with $(a,b) \in f$ and $(a,c) \in f$ implying $b = c$; $f : A \to B$, the value $f(a)$, domain and codomain,
> The natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$ (von Neumann)) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** Choice function and
The Axiom of Choice select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and The Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ (The power set $\mathcal{P}(x) = \{\, z : z \subseteq x \,\}$, The Cartesian product $A \times B := \{\, z \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(A \cup B)) : \exists a \in A\ \exists b \in B\ z = (a,b) \,\}$, The Axiom Schema of Separation: for each formula $\varphi$, $\forall \bar p\,\forall x\,\exists y\,\forall z\,(z \in y \leftrightarrow (z \in x \wedge \varphi(z,\bar p)))$); a natural is the set of its predecessors (On $\mathbb{N}$ the order is membership: $m < n \iff m \in n$). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ (Every nonzero natural number is a successor); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction (The principle of mathematical induction), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense (Chain in a poset). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, $m,\hbar>0$, and real $q,B$
with $qB\ne0$. On
$L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ close the nonnegative form
$$q_B[u]=\frac1{2m}\left(\|-i\hbar\partial_xu\|_2^2+\|(-i\hbar\partial_y-qBx)u\|_2^2\right),\qquad u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C).$$
Put $\omega_c=|qB|/m$,
$E_n=\hbar\omega_c(n+\tfrac12)$, and let $(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the
complete normalized eigenfunctions of the one-dimensional oscillator with
mass $m$, frequency $\omega_c$, and action constant $\hbar$ in its exact
self-adjoint oscillator realization. For
Schwartz $u$ define
$\mathcal F_yu(x,k)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-iky}u(x,y)\,dy$,
and use its unitary $L^2$ extension. Put $x_0(k)=\hbar k/(qB)$ and
$(Uu)(\xi,k)=\mathcal F_yu(\xi+x_0(k),k)$.
Then $U$ is unitary from $L^2(\mathbb R^2_{x,y})$ onto
$L^2(\mathbb R^2_{\xi,k})$. Writing
$$Uu(\xi,k)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty f_n(k)\psi_n(\xi),\qquad f_n\in L^2(\mathbb R_k),$$
the form closure domain and value are exactly
$$D(\overline q_B)=\left\{u:\sum_{n=0}^\infty E_n\|f_n\|_{L^2(k)}^2<\infty\right\},\qquad \overline q_B[u]=\sum_{n=0}^\infty E_n\|f_n\|_{L^2(k)}^2.$$
Thus the form is the diagonal oscillator form with an unrestricted $L^2(k)$
degeneracy factor; it asserts no finite-area state count.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, let $Q\subseteq H$ be a dense linear subspace, and let
$q:Q\times Q\to\mathbb C$ be a symmetric sesquilinear form, linear in its
first variable. Write $q[u]=q(u,u)$. Suppose that for some $c\ge0$,
$q[u]\ge-c\|u\|^2$ for every $u\in Q$, and that $Q$ is complete in the form
norm $\|u\|_{q,c}^2=q[u]+(c+1)\|u\|^2$. Then there is a unique self-adjoint
operator $H_q\ge-cI$ such that
$$D((H_q+cI)^{1/2})=Q,\qquad q(u,v)=\langle H_qu,v\rangle\quad(u\in D(H_q),\ v\in Q).$$
Equivalently, $D(H_q)$ consists exactly of those $u\in Q$ for which there is
$f\in H$ satisfying $q(u,v)=\langle f,v\rangle$ for all $v\in Q$, and then
$H_qu=f$. Under the $e^{tA}$ generator convention for associated forms, the
associated operator is $A=-H_q$. If $q_0$ is a densely defined closed symmetric
form with $q_0[u]\ge0$ and $v$ is a symmetric sesquilinear form on $Q(q_0)$
satisfying
$$|v[u,u]|\le a q_0[u]+b\|u\|^2\quad(u\in Q(q_0)),\qquad 0\le a<1,\ b\ge0,$$
then $q_0+v$ is closed and bounded below by $-b$ on the same domain. It has a
unique self-adjoint representing operator there. The form bound is not an
operator-relative bound.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix real parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$, put $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}>0$, and let $g_0,P,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite data of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$, so that $(g_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-completeness]]. Define

$$D:L^2(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dx),\qquad (Df)(x):=\ell^{-1/2}f(x/\ell),$$

and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=2n+1$, with the core $P$ and spectrum $\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]).

Then:

(a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$;

(b) the operator

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$

is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has

$$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$

where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$;

(c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$

pointwise on $\mathbb R$;

(d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$

so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

All parameters enter as positive real numbers; no physical identification of $m,\omega,\hbar$ with measured quantities is made.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

derivations.claim:
The hypotheses $m,\hbar>0$ and $qB\ne0$ make
$\omega_c=|qB|/m>0$ and the translation
$x_0(k)=\hbar k/(qB)$ well-defined. Apply [F1]: the unitary $U$ sends the
closed form to the coefficient form
$$\mathfrak q[F]=\sum_{n=0}^\infty E_n\|f_n\|_{L^2(k)}^2,$$
where $F(\xi,k)=\sum_nf_n(k)\psi_n(\xi)$ and $(\psi_n)$ is the complete
oscillator basis from [F3]. In particular,
$\mathfrak q[F]\ge E_0\|F\|_2^2>0$ for nonzero $F$.

Apply the closed-form representation theorem [F2] to the normalized form
$\widehat{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/E_{\mathrm{ref}}$. If $F=(f_n)$ is in
its representing operator domain, there is $G=(g_n)$ in the coefficient
Hilbert space such that $\widehat{\mathfrak q}(F,V)=\langle G,V\rangle$
for every form-domain vector $V$. Fix $n$ and take $V$ to have sole nonzero
component $V_n=(E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})f_n-g_n$. It lies in the form domain
because $f_n,g_n\in L^2(k)$ and $E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is finite. The
representation identity gives
$$0=\widehat{\mathfrak q}(F,V)-\langle G,V\rangle=\|(E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})f_n-g_n\|_2^2,$$
so $g_n=(E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})f_n$ for every $n$. Since $G$ belongs to the
Hilbert space, $\sum_n(E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})^2\|f_n\|_2^2<\infty$,
equivalently $\sum_nE_n^2\|f_n\|_2^2<\infty$ because
$E_{\mathrm{ref}}>0$.

Conversely, suppose $F$ is in the form domain and
$\sum_nE_n^2\|f_n\|_2^2<\infty$. Define
$G_n=(E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})f_n$, which is a vector in the coefficient
Hilbert space. For every form-domain vector $V=(v_n)$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives
absolute convergence and
$$\widehat{\mathfrak q}(F,V)=\sum_n(E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})\langle f_n,v_n\rangle=\sum_n\langle G_n,v_n\rangle=\langle G,V\rangle.$$
Thus [F2] represents the normalized operator by
$(f_n)\mapsto((E_n/E_{\mathrm{ref}})f_n)$ on the stated domain. The model
Hamiltonian is $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$ times this operator and therefore acts by
$(f_n)\mapsto(E_nf_n)$ on that same domain; uniqueness identifies it with
the postulated Hamiltonian.

For each $n$, the eigenspace at $E_n$ is
$L^2(\mathbb R_k)\otimes\mathbb C\psi_n$, which is infinite-dimensional;
the energies are strictly increasing and tend to $+\infty$. If
$z\notin\{E_n:n\ge0\}$, then $\inf_n|E_n-z|>0$ and
$\sup_n E_n/|E_n-z|<\infty$. The diagonal inverse is therefore bounded and
maps into the operator domain, so $z$ is in the resolvent. Each $E_n$ is an
eigenvalue, and the complete coefficient decomposition together with [F4]
shows that all spectral projections are sums of eigenspace projections.
Hence every spectral measure is atomic on the displayed set and the spectrum
is exactly that set.

derivations.claim: In the standard orthonormal wedge basis from [F4], the matrix entry of $\bigwedge^m T$ in row $I$, column $J$ is $\det T_{I,J}$ by [F3]. Consequently $[(\bigwedge^mT)^*]_{I,J}=\overline{\det T_{J,I}}=\det (T^*)_{I,J}$, so $(\bigwedge^mT)^*=\bigwedge^m(T^*)$. Applying this to $P=P^*$ shows $Q=Q^*$.

Functoriality [F2] gives $Q^2=\bigwedge^m(P^2)=\bigwedge^mP=Q$. Hence $Q$ is a Hermitian idempotent by step 1.1; for $x=Qy$ and $Qz=0$, $\langle x,z\rangle=\langle Qy,z\rangle=\langle y,Qz\rangle=0$, so its range and kernel are orthogonal and it is the orthogonal projection onto its range.

Every decomposable wedge in the image of $Q$ is a wedge of $m$ vectors in $\operatorname{im}P$, so the full image lies in $\bigwedge^m\operatorname{im}P$. Conversely, for a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_m$ of the $m$-dimensional range of $P$, $Q(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_m)=v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_m\ne0$. The increasing-wedge basis theorem [F4], applied to this basis of the range, says $\bigwedge^m\operatorname{im}P$ is one-dimensional; thus it equals $\operatorname{im}Q$ and $Q$ has rank one.

Each matrix entry of $Q(x)$ is a polynomial minor in the entries of $P(x)$ by [F3], hence is $C^2$. Together with step 2.1 this proves that $Q$ is a $C^2$ rank-one orthogonal projector with the stated range, and its ranges form the determinant line subbundle.

citations.quote:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is defined by the same bounded tensor maps and is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately. The finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment described by the finite open-system postulate is for $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$ with a fixed environment state and a declared joint unitary; it may be used for a separately selected finite-dimensional subsystem but does not cover the Fock field. A reduced-dynamics model involving the Fock field must separately specify a trace-class joint preparation and joint unitary on $\mathcal H_{AF}$. The trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)}:\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_{AF})\to\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_A)$ is defined for arbitrary Hilbert factors, is trace-norm contractive, and preserves positivity and trace by the mathematical partial-trace result listed below. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, fix a positive real action-scale parameter
$\hbar>0$, and let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.

Assume AC, $r\ge1$, and the finite-mode Fock conventions of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Let $U,V\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ obey
$$UU^*-VV^*=I_r,\qquad UV^T=VU^T,$$
where $^*$ is conjugate transpose and $^T$ is transpose without conjugation.
On the finite Hermite core define
$$a'_j=\sum_k(U_{jk}a_k+V_{jk}a_k^*).$$
Then the $a'_j$ satisfy $[a'_j,(a'_k)^*]=\delta_{jk}I$ and
$[a'_j,a'_k]=0$ on that core. The real matrix
$$S_g=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}(U+V)&-\operatorname{Im}(U-V)\\ \operatorname{Im}(U+V)&\operatorname{Re}(U-V)\end{pmatrix}$$
is symplectic in grouped coordinate order $(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r)$.
There is a unitary $M$ on finite-mode Fock, obtained by transporting an
individual finite symplectic implementer through the Fock–Schrödinger
unitary, such that $M^*aM=a'$ on the transported Schwartz core and
$M^*W(z)M=W(S_g^Tz)$ in grouped Weyl-label order. The transformed vacuum
$M\Omega$ has finite mean number
$$\sum_j\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=\operatorname{tr}(VV^*).$$
No infinite-mode implementability assertion is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

derivations.claim: The matrix $C$ is unitary because $C^*C=I_2$ follows from $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$. Its transpose $S=C^T$ is also unitary, so $U=S,V=0$ satisfy $UU^*-VV^*=I_2$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. By [F2] the finite-mode Bogoliubov statement supplies an implementer $M$ with $M^*aM=Sa$. Multiplying by $M$ and $M^*$ gives $MaM^*=S^{-1}a$; taking adjoints gives $Ma^*M^*=\overline{S}^{-1}a^*=S^Ta^*=Ca^*$ because $S$ is unitary and $S^T=C$. These identities hold on the transported finite-particle core.

The transformed vacuum has $\sum_{j=1}^2\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=0$ by [F2], so $a_1M\Omega=a_2M\Omega=0$. Expanding $M\Omega$ in the complete occupation basis [F1], the equation $a_1\psi=0$ forces every coefficient with first occupation $n_1>0$ to vanish by the ladder formula; $a_2\psi=0$ then forces every coefficient with $n_2>0$ to vanish. Hence $M\Omega=e^{i\phi}\Omega$ for some real $\phi$. Replacing $M$ by $U_C=e^{-i\phi}M$ preserves the conjugation identities and gives $U_C\Omega=\Omega$.

For $|n,0\rangle=(a_1^*)^n\Omega/\sqrt{n!}$, repeated use of the creation identity in [F1], the conjugation identity from step 1.1, and $U_C\Omega=\Omega$ from step 2.1 give $U_C|n,0\rangle=(t a_1^*+r a_2^*)^n\Omega/\sqrt{n!}=\sum_{k=0}^n\sqrt{\binom nk}t^k r^{n-k}|k,n-k\rangle$. The coefficient follows by choosing which $k$ of the $n$ commuting creation factors contribute $a_1^*$ and using $|k,n-k\rangle=(a_1^*)^k(a_2^*)^{n-k}\Omega/\sqrt{k!(n-k)!}$.

Orthogonality of the output occupation basis makes the joint ideal number-count probability the squared modulus of the coefficient in step 3.1. Since $|t|^2=\eta$ and $|r|^2=1-\eta$, for $0<\eta<1$ this is the displayed binomial law; at the endpoints the expansion has a single surviving basis vector. The declared number PVM and its Born rule [A1, F4] assign these probabilities.

By [F1, F3, F5], the families $|m,n\rangle$ and $|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$ are complete orthonormal families in $\mathcal F^{(2)}$ and $\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$, respectively. On finite sums define $\mathcal J_0\sum c_{mn}|m,n\rangle=\sum c_{mn}|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$; orthonormality makes its squared norm $\sum|c_{mn}|^2$, so it is well defined and inner-product preserving. For $\psi\in\mathcal F^{(2)}$, approximate by finite sums $\psi_j$ and define $\mathcal J\psi=\lim_j\mathcal J_0\psi_j$. The norm identity makes the images Cauchy in the complete product and the limit independent of the approximating sequence; it preserves linearity, norm and inner product. Its range is closed: if $\mathcal J\psi_j$ converges, the same norm identity makes $\psi_j$ Cauchy in the complete Fock space, so its limit maps to that range limit. The range contains the complete product family and hence is dense, so it is the whole product. This proves that $\mathcal J$ is unitary, uniquely fixed by the occupation map, with $\mathcal J\Omega=|0\rangle\otimes|0\rangle$. The coherent input series converges by [F3] and this unitary identification. Apply the bounded unitary $U_C$ to its norm-convergent partial sums. Each output occupation coefficient has only one contributing input total $n=k+\ell$; step 3.1 gives it as $e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\alpha^{k+\ell}t^kr^\ell/\sqrt{k!\ell!}$. The product of the two norm-convergent coherent series exists in the completed product by [F5]; approximating each factor by finite partial sums is legitimate since $\|u\otimes v-u'\otimes v'\|\le\|u-u'\|\|v\|+\|u'\|\|v-v'\|$. Its product-basis coefficients are the same, because $|t\alpha|^2+|r\alpha|^2=|\alpha|^2$. Completeness of that basis therefore proves $\mathcal J U_C|\alpha,0\rangle=|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$, retaining the exact vacuum phase and port convention.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. The mode operators are dimensionless and on the finite-particle core satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

The assigned dipole interaction core expression is $V_{\mathrm{dip}}=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_jD_j\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)$ in the ordered space $\mathcal H_A\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$; each summand has units joules and acts on the finite-particle core. This clause assigns the finite matrix expression only. It does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generate an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_A\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h))$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a state $\rho$, the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $Q_j$ is the self-adjoint quadrature fixed by [[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on the finite-particle core equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately; the optional finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment has the exact scope of the finite open-system postulate and implies no reservoir limit.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.

Assume AC, $r\ge1$, and the finite-mode Fock conventions of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Let $U,V\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ obey
$$UU^*-VV^*=I_r,\qquad UV^T=VU^T,$$
where $^*$ is conjugate transpose and $^T$ is transpose without conjugation.
On the finite Hermite core define
$$a'_j=\sum_k(U_{jk}a_k+V_{jk}a_k^*).$$
Then the $a'_j$ satisfy $[a'_j,(a'_k)^*]=\delta_{jk}I$ and
$[a'_j,a'_k]=0$ on that core. The real matrix
$$S_g=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}(U+V)&-\operatorname{Im}(U-V)\\ \operatorname{Im}(U+V)&\operatorname{Re}(U-V)\end{pmatrix}$$
is symplectic in grouped coordinate order $(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r)$.
There is a unitary $M$ on finite-mode Fock, obtained by transporting an
individual finite symplectic implementer through the Fock–Schrödinger
unitary, such that $M^*aM=a'$ on the transported Schwartz core and
$M^*W(z)M=W(S_g^Tz)$ in grouped Weyl-label order. The transformed vacuum
$M\Omega$ has finite mean number
$$\sum_j\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=\operatorname{tr}(VV^*).$$
No infinite-mode implementability assertion is made.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.
